source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Reproductive Health (Male & Female)
questions.stem: The structure left in the ovary after the mature ovum is released is the:
questions.rationale: After ovulation the follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 123)
questions.quote: Corpus luteum is the structure left aner the mature ovum is discharged.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: A normal umbilical cord contains:
questions.rationale: The cord has two arteries and one vein (AVA); a single artery may signal anomalies.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 123)
questions.quote: Ihe umbilical cord is composed of 2 arteries and I vein.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: A woman's obstetric score is G5 P3114. How many preterm births has she had?
questions.rationale: After G5, TPAL = Term 3, Preterm 1, Abortion 1, Living 4.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 123)
questions.quote: Gravida 5 Para 3 t 1 4 means that the woman had 5 pregnancies, 3 term deliveries. I preterm delive , I abortion, and 4 livin children.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: A woman at 8 weeks reports amenorrhea, breast tenderness and a positive urine test. These findings are best classified as:
questions.rationale: Amenorrhea and breast changes are presumptive; a positive test is probable. Positive signs are fetal heart tones, fetal movement felt by examiner and fetal outline.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 123)
questions.quote: Absence of menstruation and quickening are resum tive si nsof re nanc

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Using Naegele's rule, the expected date of delivery for a last menstrual period beginning May 10 is:
questions.rationale: Subtract 3 months, add 7 days, add 1 year: May 10 → February 17.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: From the last normal menstrual period, subtract 3 from the month, add 7 for the day, and add I year.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: A pregnant woman feels faint while lying on her back. The nurse helps her to lie:
questions.rationale: Left lateral position relieves compression of the inferior vena cava by the uterus (supine hypotension).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: This position relieves compression of the inferior vena cava by the gravid utens.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Which advice helps a woman with morning sickness in the first trimester?
questions.rationale: Small frequent meals, dry crackers, low-fat food and fluids between meals help; no drugs without prescription.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: To relieve nausea and vomiting during the first trimester, woman is to take dry toast or crackers.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is elevated. This may indicate:
questions.rationale: AFP is measured from maternal blood; high levels suggest open neural tube defects.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: High of AFP may indicate-presence of neural tube defect (e. . S ina bifida)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: To prevent toxoplasmosis, a pregnant woman should avoid:
questions.rationale: Toxoplasmosis comes from raw meat and cat feces; it crosses the placenta and can cause hydrocephalus or chorioretinitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: Toxoplasmosis is an infection contacted through eating raw meats or handling cat litters.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman with severe gestational hypertension is at increased risk of:
questions.rationale: Hypertension impairs uteroplacental circulation and predisposes to premature placental separation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: Abruptio placenta, which is premature separation of nonnally implanted placenta in the third trimester is a potential complication of PIH

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding supports abruptio placentae rather than placenta previa?
options: Rising fundal height and rigid uterus
questions.rationale: Abruption causes painful bleeding, board-like uterus and rising fundus from concealed bleeding; previa is painless with a soft uterus.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: A manifestation is rising ftndal height from blood trapped behind placenta.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which sign should be posted at the bedside of a client with placenta previa?
questions.rationale: The placenta lies over or near the os; vaginal or internal examination can cause massive bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: nursing intervention should include avoidance of invasive procedures like vaginal examination

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The presenting part is 2 cm below the ischial spines. The station is:
questions.rationale: Station 0 is at the spines; below is positive, above is negative.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 125)
questions.quote: If the presenting part of the fetus is at 2 cm. below the ischial spine, it is station (+) 2.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: During the first Leopold maneuver, the nurse feels a hard, round, movable part in the fundus. The presentation is:
questions.rationale: The first maneuver identifies the part in the fundus; if the head is there, the buttocks present (breech).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 125)
questions.quote: The head is hard, round, and movable. Therefore the resentation is breech

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which finding indicates false labor?
options: Contractions ease with walking or rest
Back pain not relieved by walking
questions.rationale: False labor contractions are irregular and decrease; true labor causes progressive dilatation and effacement.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 125)
questions.quote: Contractions that decrease in duration and intensity is false labor.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which contraction pattern in active labor needs immediate follow-up?
questions.rationale: Contractions longer than 90 seconds or closer than 2 minutes risk tetanic contractions, uterine rupture and fetal hypoxia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 125)
questions.quote: Uterine contractions that last more than 90 seconds and with frequency of less than 2 minutes leads to tetanic contractions.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Fetal heart rate decelerations begin with the start of each contraction and mirror it. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Early decelerations = head compression; variable = cord compression; late = uteroplacental insufficiency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: Early deceleration indicates head compression; variable deceleration indicates cord compression

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: After rupture of membranes, the nurse sees the umbilical cord at the vulva. Which action is inappropriate?
options: Pushing the cord back into the uterus
Lifting the presenting part with gloved fingers
questions.rationale: Do not replace the cord; relieve pressure on it with positioning and manual elevation of the presenting part.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: When prolapse of the cord occurs; pushing the cord into the uterus is an inappropriate nursing action.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: During an oxytocin infusion, the fetal monitor shows signs of fetal distress. The nurse first:
options: Lays the mother flat on her back
questions.rationale: Stop oxytocin, turn to the left side, give oxygen and prepare for possible cesarean.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: During fetal distress, Pitocin drip should be discontinued.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Four hours after delivery, the fundus is at the umbilicus and deviated to the right. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: A full bladder displaces the uterus and impairs contraction, increasing bleeding risk; help her void.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 127)
questions.quote: Deviation of the fundus of the uterus to the side of the abdomen indicates distended bladder.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: A mother with a perineal hematoma after a forceps delivery should first receive:
options: Ice packs for the first 24 hours
Warm sitz baths in the first 24 hours
questions.rationale: Cold causes vasoconstriction and limits bleeding; warmth in the first 24 hours increases bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 127)
questions.quote: ice application for the first 24 hours to promote vasoconstriction and to prevent bleeding

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: On her 4th postpartum day, a mother starts doing things for herself and wants to learn baby care. She is in Rubin's:
questions.rationale: Taking-hold (about days 3–10): more independent, eager to learn mothering tasks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 127)
questions.quote: Taking-hold phase is characterized by the following: mother becomes more independent; she begins to assume tasks of mothering.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A postpartum client has thrombophlebitis of the leg. Which action needs correction?
questions.rationale: Massage may dislodge a clot and cause pulmonary embolism.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 128)
questions.quote: Massaging the legs ofa client with thrombophlebitis may dislodge blood clots that will lead to pulmonary embolism.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: When preterm delivery cannot be stopped, betamethasone is given to the mother to:
questions.rationale: Antenatal corticosteroids increase fetal surfactant production and improve survival.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 128)
questions.quote: This medication increases surfactant production and thereby. increasing probability of the fetus to survive.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client on terbutaline to stop preterm labor should be monitored for:
questions.rationale: Terbutaline is a beta-agonist: tachycardia, palpitations, tremors, nervousness.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 128)
questions.quote: tachycardia, nervousness, tremors, headache, itations,arrh ias, and hy rtension.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used as eye prophylaxis for the newborn against gonococcal and chlamydial conjunctivitis?
questions.rationale: Erythromycin (or tetracycline) ointment is used for neonatal eye prophylaxis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 128)
questions.quote: Erythromycin and tetracycline are the medications used as eye prophylaxis for gonorrhea and chlamydia.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Reproductive Health (Male & Female)
questions.stem: Before a 24-year-old starts combined oral contraceptive pills, the nurse should check especially for:
questions.rationale: Estrogen can raise BP and clotting risk; hypertension and thrombophlebitis are contraindications.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 128)
questions.quote: Before starting oral contraceptives, the nurse should assess the client for signs and symptoms of hypertension.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: In the first trimester a woman says, "I'm not sure I want to be pregnant with all these discomforts." The nurse recognizes this as:
questions.rationale: Ambivalence is normal in the first trimester; acceptance usually follows.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Maternity exercises (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: During the first trimester, it is normal for the pregnant woman to experience ambivalence.
